That or at least slow waaaayyyy down. Speed will come on its own with practice and training, but you should never have any symptoms of fainting, basically.

I was always a great sprinter, but an awful distance runner, I ended up buying a gps watch when I decided that I'd find a way to be able to run long distances, and I found out that my "slow easy run" was actually like a 6 minute mile.

Sure, it was slow compared to the sprints I was used to, but there was no way I was going to be able to maintain a 6 minute mile for any semi-long period with 0 training... You may just lack the context to realize how hard you're pushing yourself, I certainly did.

If you don't mind running with a phone, you can check your pace on a free running app, id say aim for a slow pace like 10, 11, 12 minute miles, even slower if you have to (a half marathon around me has a minimum pace of 16 minutes/mile, basically walking briskly... Don't think you have to be fast from day 1), and see how that feels.

Having said that, if you can get a stress test, maybe it's not a bad idea, just in case. I don't think most people get blurred vision even when they're new to running. You may be pushing yourself too hard, but if you can play it safe and get a test, it may be good. I wouldn't freak out or anything, by the way, I'm just saying if you can get a stress test, it's probably not the worst idea in the world just to make sure everything's fine and you're just pushing yourself beyond your temporary limits because you're not trained to that level yet.
